sample_unit: intake notes (parseable LLM outputs); 50 notes in human-rater validation

links.outcome: LLM extraction agreement with human raters on local historical intake notes versus human-only reliability
links.effect: Human-plus-LLM reliability did not differ significantly from human-only reliability (human κ 0.71–0.94; human-plus-LLM κ 0.70–0.93) across measures.
links.quote: In detected-vs-not-detected coding, human-plus-LLM reliability did not differ significantly from human-only reliability across measures (human κ, 0.71–0.94; human-plus-LLM κ, 0.70–0.93).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM classifications across 50 repeated calls per note and its relation to human agreement
links.effect: Mean LLM-human agreement rose from 42.6% for classifications with <80% stability to 82.7% for 100% stability (Pearson r=0.36).
links.quote: Stability was associated with human agreement: mean LLM-human agreement increased from 42.6% for classifications with <80% stability to 82.7% for 100% stability (Pearson r=0.36).

unlisted_practices: Local hosting of open-weight LLM to keep clinical notes in-house for extraction

screen.reason: Evaluated a locally hosted open-weight LLM for clinical NLP/chart review and tested repeated-query stability across 50 independent calls per note to measure reliability and correlation with human agreement.
